official.deadline_note: There is no single MOE deadline: the window depends on the applicant's qualification type. Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' Level closes 19 March 2027; International Baccalaureate and international/other qualifications open mid-October 2026; NUS High School Diploma opens early December 2026; Polytechnic Diploma opens early February 2027. The PSC-administered PSC Scholarship (Teaching Service) for 2027 closes earlier, on 15 March 2027.
official.application_cycle: PSC Scholarships for 2027 (open, closing 15 March 2027); MOE windows timed to the 2027 school-leaver and A-Level results release
official.status_note: PSC Scholarships for 2027 are open and close 15 March 2027. On the MOE application page, the Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' Level window opens on the date of the GCE A-Level results release and runs to 19 March 2027; the International Baccalaureate and international/other qualifications window opens mid-October 2026; the NUS High School Diploma window opens early December 2026; and the Polytechnic Diploma window opens early February 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: MOE states 'Full coverage of your undergraduate tuition fees' and, in the scholarship/award details, 'Tuition fees and other approved charges' for both the Public Service Commission-administered Education Merit Scholarship/Teaching Scholarship and the MOE-administered Teaching Award.

A monthly allowance to support your expenses during your studies
Exclusive developmental opportunities tailored to nurture educational leaders
Opportunity to enrol in the specially curated NTU-NIE Bachelor of Arts/Science (BABSc) programme
Tuition fees and other approved charges
Return economy airfare, if you are studying overseas
Developmental programmes, during your undergraduate studies
Approved student exchange programmes, summer programmes and CCAs
Possibility of sponsorship of Master's degree (if requirements are met)

A well-rounded individual with good academic and co-curricular activities (CCA) records
GCE A-Level, International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma or equivalent
Possesses excellent interpersonal and communication skills

PSC Scholarship (Teaching Service) applicants must also be a Singapore Citizen, demonstrate strong leadership qualities and potential, and present themselves as well-rounded individuals with good academic and non-academic records
requirements: All applicants will be considered for the full range of MOE Teaching Scholarships and Award
Study at a reputable local or overseas university (scholarship route) or reputable local universities including the NTU-NIE BABSc programme (award route)
Course of study should be of relevance to a teaching subject such as Art and Music, Humanities, Languages, Mathematics, Physical Education and Sports Science, Sciences or Social Sciences
Applicants who wish to pursue other similar courses of study may still apply; MOE will advise subsequently on the subject(s) they can be assigned to teach
Shortlisted applicants will be invited for an interview and may be scheduled for other selection processes as well
documents: The application process will require interested candidates to submit an online application form, complete with the necessary supporting documents (MOE)
Secondary 4 / Year 4 year-end school academic reports (including results and teachers' comments) - PSC Scholarship route
Secondary 4 / Year 4 CCA and Community Involvement Programme (CIP) records - PSC Scholarship route
Pre-tertiary CCA and CIP records - PSC Scholarship route

Certificates of academic qualification obtained (e.g. GCE O-level, GCE A-level, IB Diploma, NUS High School Diploma, Polytechnic Diploma, other high school diploma or equivalent); preliminary examination results need not be included - PSC Scholarship route
An essay accompanying the application form, plus a video interview completed after submission - PSC Scholarship route
selection_criteria: Well-rounded individual with good academic and co-curricular activities (CCA) records
Relevance of the course of study to a teaching subject
Shortlisted applicants attend an interview and may be scheduled for other selection processes
PSC route adds psychometric assessments, game-based assessments and a psychological interview before a panel interview with the Public Service Commission (PSC) Scholarships Selection Board
coverage: Tuition fees and other approved charges
Return economy airfare, if you are studying overseas
Approved student exchange programmes, summer programmes and CCAs
Possibility of sponsorship of a Master's degree (if requirements are met)
Full coverage of your undergraduate tuition fees and a monthly allowance to support your expenses during your studies
application_method: Apply directly to MOE via the links published on the MOE application page during the relevant application window
Submit an online application form, complete with the necessary supporting documents
Candidates interested in the Public Service Commission Scholarship (Teaching Service) apply via the PSC Gateway Portal, logging in with Singpass
Join the MOE Careers mailing list to receive email updates on MOE scholarships-related events
official.application_route: Apply directly to MOE online during the qualification-specific window (Singapore-Cambridge GCE 'A' Level, International Baccalaureate/international qualifications, NUS High School Diploma or Polytechnic Diploma); for the PSC-administered Education Merit Scholarship/Teaching Scholarship, apply through the PSC Gateway Portal with Singpass.
official.citizenship_residency: Singapore Citizen at point of offer
official.international_eligibility: Not eligible - applicants must be Singapore Citizens at the point of offer
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The course of study should be of relevance to a teaching subject, such as Art and Music, Humanities, Languages, Mathematics, Physical Education and Sports Science, Sciences or Social Sciences
official.duration: Full-time undergraduate degree, with a bond of 4 years for local studies, 5 years for studies in non-English speaking countries and 6 years for studies in English speaking countries; a further 3-year bond applies if enrolled in the Postgraduate Diploma in Education (PGDE) programme at NIE, concurrent with the scholarship bond. The bond period starts on the day the scholar assumes official duty after completing studies and NIE training (if applicable).
official.description: MOE states that it is dedicated to nurturing the next generation of educational leaders and provides varied opportunities for aspiring educators through its teaching scholarships/award. All scholars and award holders receive sponsorship for their undergraduate tuition fees and other approved programmes, a maintenance allowance, and the opportunity to undergo MOE developmental programmes to prepare them as future educators.
official.program_type: MOE Teaching Scholarships and Award (Full-Term), undergraduate; administered either by the Public Service Commission (Education Merit Scholarship / Teaching Scholarship) or by MOE (Teaching Award)

verification.notes: Checked the MOE overview, Scholarship and Award details and Application pages (last updated 20 Jan 2026, 30 Jul 2026 and 14 Sep 2026 respectively) plus the MOE teaching-scholarships hub page and the Public Service Commission undergraduate scholarships, apply and Teaching Service pages. Benefit wording, eligibility, bond, application windows, deadlines and required documents were taken verbatim-in-meaning from those pages. MOE publishes no allowance figure anywhere on these pages, so funding_amount and funding_currency are null; fully_funded is set true only because MOE itself states full coverage of undergraduate tuition fees, a monthly allowance to support expenses during studies, and return economy airfare when studying overseas.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a bonded teaching pathway, not a cash award: you are paid to train and then owe MOE four to six years of service depending on where you studied. Decide early which qualification window governs you, because MOE runs four separate windows (A-Level results release to 19 March 2027, IB/international from mid-October 2026, NUS High from early December 2026, polytechnic from early February 2027) and the PSC Teaching Service route shuts a week earlier on 15 March 2027. Your intended degree must map onto a school teaching subject, and your co-curricular record carries as much weight as your grades. If you are accepted onto the NTU-NIE Bachelor of Arts/Science you graduate already qualified to teach and skip the PGDE entirely.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizen school leavers (A-Level, IB, polytechnic diploma or NUS High Diploma) with strong all-round academic, CCA and leadership records who are already sure they want to teach in a Singapore school and will accept a 4-6 year bond.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify which of the four qualification windows applies to you and diarise the opening date, not just the closing date
For the PSC Teaching Service route, activate and test your Singpass login before the window opens
Pull Secondary 4 / Year 4 year-end reports with results and teachers' comments, and assemble CCA/CIP records from both Secondary 4 and the pre-tertiary years
Check that your chosen degree maps to a teaching subject (Art and Music, Humanities, Languages, Mathematics, PE and Sports Science, Sciences, Social Sciences)
Draft the PSC essay and prepare for a video interview that must be completed within 7 days of submitting
Join the MOE Careers mailing list for window-opening reminders and scholarship events
common_rejection_risks: A thin co-curricular or leadership record: MOE screens for a well-rounded individual, so strong grades alone are not sufficient
Choosing a degree with no clear teaching-subject relevance, leaving assessors unable to place you
Submitting late in the window, when interview slots have already been scheduled for earlier applicants

On the PSC route, leaving the essay, a supporting document or the video interview unfinished - the application is only counted as complete when the form, essay and all documents are submitted and the video interview is done
Applying through the wrong administrator: MOE and PSC are separate portals with separate deadlines, and a MOE submission does not put you forward for the PSC scholarships
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: MOE and PSC publish no allowance figures, so you cannot verify from the official pages whether the monthly maintenance allowance covers your actual living costs; assume you must fund personal and non-approved expenses yourself. For overseas study, only return economy airfare is provided - relocation, accommodation deposits, visa and settling-in costs beyond approved charges are not stated as covered.
document_audit: Secondary 4 / Year 4 reports must include both results and teachers' comments - a bare results slip is not what PSC asks for
Do not include preliminary examination results; PSC explicitly says they are not needed
CCA and CIP records are asked for at two separate stages (Secondary 4 and pre-tertiary) - missing either creates a gap
The PSC application portal is not supported on mobile devices or tablets; use a laptop or desktop
The video interview link arrives within about 7 days of submission, so monitor the email and spam folder
Male Singaporean applicants should expect National Service status to be part of the picture, though neither MOE nor PSC states NS wording on these pages
alerts: All four MOE windows are staggered by qualification type, and two of them (polytechnic, NUS High) do not open until February and December - missing your slot means waiting a full cycle
MOE explicitly warns against waiting until the end of the window, because shortlisted early applicants are scheduled for interviews sooner
The bond is 4 years for local study, 5 years for non-English-speaking countries and 6 years for English-speaking countries, and it starts the day you assume duty after graduation and NIE training
If you take the PGDE at NIE you pick up an additional 3-year bond, concurrent with the scholarship bond - the BABSc route avoids this

You can be offered either the PSC-administered Education Merit Scholarship/Teaching Scholarship or the MOE-administered Teaching Award, and the two have different country-of-study and benefit sets (overseas study and possible Master's sponsorship sit with the PSC-administered scholarships)

Silence is not rejection: PSC states you may still be under active consideration, and MOE states that not hearing within 3 weeks after your interview means your application is still being actively considered
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online in your qualification-specific window, upload documents, then wait for MOE or PSC to shortlist you into interviews, psychometric/game-based/psychological assessments and finally a panel board.
